text:
nina (AE): Quick sync — BrightMart wants a 3-day POC. Goals: browser streaming chat, server-side Python processor that calls our toolkit functions for inventory checks, and strictly validated JSON events for their ETL. They're sensitive to cost and asked for SOC2/KMS details up front. Who can own tech?
leo (SE): I can own the tech flow. Need to confirm whether the browser will use SSE or websocket. They prefer minimal client deps, so SSE would be ideal if we can demo function calls over it.
nana (Eng): Function-calling over SSE is fine — endpoints are the same. We should demo two modes: 1) streaming websocket with binary ping/keepalive for low-latency, 2) SSE fallback for simple clients.
leo (SE): Good. Also they want deterministic JSON outputs, e.g., an order_event schema. I'll prepare validation using our function_call pattern so the model returns a single function invocation with args matching the schema.
taylor (DevEx): I'll put together tiny example repos: node client + SSE shim, node websocket sample, and python consumer that validates and forwards events. Sample schema I'll include:
```json
{"order_event":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"sku":{"type":"string"},"qty":{"type":"integer"}}}},"total_cents":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["order_id","items","total_cents"]}
```
leo (SE): Add a snippet showing server-side enforcement using our function_call route: call name "emit_order_event" and validate args with JSON Schema on the server. If schema mismatches, return structured error and request model retry.
nana (Eng): Performance note: token accounting for streamed conversations + metadata. For a checkout flow expect ~300-420 tokens per transaction depending on context window. If they're hitting 120 TPS for short spikes, hosted pricing balloons. Recommend offering a short-term dedicated trial (48h burst credits) or a committed dev pool. I'll draft two cost scenarios.
security-bot: Received their security questionnaire. Items flagged: EU data residency, HSM/KMS integration, log retention window, and whether chat content is used for model tuning. They asked for SOC2 report and encryption details.
legal: We'll need to review their DPA and propose a POC addendum with data TTL and log scoping. Also confirm no PII in sample transactions or mask by default. We can turn the addendum in ~48 hours.
nina (AE): Sales wants a simple per-checkout ballpark for the kickoff. They asked: websockets streaming, function call to inventory, structured JSON output, 2h/day at spike levels (120 TPS) for 3 days. Can we get a rough number before EOD?
nana (Eng): Quick napkin calc: assume 360 tokens per checkout avg. Peak tokens/sec = 120 * 360 = 43,200 tok/s. For 2h/day over 3 days: 43,200 * 3600 * 2 * 3 = 933,120,000 tokens. Hosted cost at $0.0004/token (example) would be $373,248 — clearly not acceptable. With dedicated quantized variant and batching we can reduce ~5x. With a temporary dedicated dev pool + burst credits estimate ~ $60k for the 3-day window. I'll make a spreadsheet with three options: hosted (not recommended), dedicated trial (recommended), and hybrid (edge route + fallback).
leo (SE): I'll produce a short runbook for the customer kickoff: 1) enable EU region, 2) generate ephemeral creds, 3) run canary script to exercise emit_order_event, 4) validate JSON schema and fallback to server post-processing, 5) capture logs to secure bucket with TTL. Include sample curl/ws commands and sample canary output.
taylor (DevEx): Repos will include: README, quickstart, canary script, schema validator, and a troubleshooting doc for common streaming issues (CORS, proxies, idle timeouts, reconnect strategies). I'll include a small automated test that asserts the model returns exactly one function call per checkout.
security-bot: We'll prepare the KMS/HSM and SOC2 answers within 24 hours and recommend using EU-only region for data-in-transit & at-rest. Will provide recommended retention window for logs.
legal: Confirmed — we can supply a POC addendum template and non-prod data handling language. Requesting AE to confirm whether any real customer PII will be used during the trial.
nina (AE): They said they will use anonymized test orders only. Good. Action items:
- leo: tech runbook + canary script by EOD (participant: leo)
- nana: pricing spreadsheet with 3 scenarios by EOD (participant: ana)
- taylor: sample repos + schema + troubleshooting by EOD (participant: taylor)
- security-bot: answered questionnaire snippets in 24h
- legal: POC addendum template in 48h

leo (SE): I'll also attach a tiny validation snippet in the runbook showing server-side JSON Schema check and how to reject/ask the model to reemit. Example pseudo:```js
if (!validate(schema, payload)) { return {error: 'schema_mismatch', action: 'retry_with_clarifying_prompt'} } else { emit(payload) }
```
nana (Eng): I'll include an alternate config recommending our quantized LLM variant + prefix caching to reduce tokens. Also note function-call enforcement avoids downstream parsing surprises.
taylor (DevEx): Republishing repos to the sales-drive once ready and will drop links here.
nina (AE): Thanks all — I'll tentatively book kickoff Tue 09:00 CET and update BrightMart. :thumbsup:
